newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA INTERIM PM PROPOSES PEGGING LEV TO MARK.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA INTERIM PM PROPOSES PEGGING LEV TO MARK.

text.p: Bulgaria's Financial Stabilisation Council advising the interim cabinet proposed on Monday pegging the lev to the mark as anchor currency in a fixed exchange rate regime aimed at restoring confidence in the financial system, interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski said.
"We would recommend to peg the lev to the mark, but I would like to stress that it is up to the new government and parliament to take the final decision," Sofianski told reporters.

Bulgaria has pledged to introduce a restrictive monetary system known as a currency board by mid-year. Under the system the lev will be pegged to an anchor currency, at a rate that cannot be adjusted, and the amount of levs in circulation must be matched precisely by foreign exchange reserves.
An International Monetary Fund mission is currently in Sofia to discuss final preparations for its introduction.

Bulgaria's prime minister designate Ivan Kostov, leader of the Union of Democratic Forces, was formally asked by President Petar Stoyanov last week to form a government following his party's victory in April 19 elections. Kostov will present the new cabinet to parliament on Wednesday. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
